hook: SCP-004 is an old barn door on an abandoned factory and a ring of twelve rusted keys, each of which opens the same door onto a different place. Much of it is told as a dated timeline, so it reads like a case history more than a standard report. Be ready for blunt body horror early on: most of the keys tear whoever walks through into scattered pieces.
whyItMatters: The premise of one door whose destination depends on the key is simple enough to explain in a sentence, and the article gets a great deal out of it. It is also a piece of setting-building, since the Foundation ends up treating the impossible room behind the door as real estate. The terse, heavily redacted style leaves gaps that the reader fills in, which is part of its unease.
thingsToNotice:
The first death sets the tone: a boy opens the door with the wrong key and is ripped apart, his right hand turning up eight kilometers away and other parts as far as 32 km off. Ten of the twelve D-class sent through on day one die the same way, and the Foundation's answer to the witnesses is to terminate the surviving boys and the sheriff they called. Decades later, the missing remains of the boy and of one test subject reappear at the door still warm, their blood not yet clotted, which is the clearest sign that time behaves badly here.

The one safe key, 004-7, opens an unmeasurable dark room, and the Foundation's ambition turns it into Site-62, a bunker meant to hold emergency stock, mobile anomalies and a backup of its entire database. Because of the time slippage the staff are kept on site for good, and their families are told they died in an industrial accident and buried cloned bodies. Then a 53-minute blackout leaves everyone sensing humanoid creatures in the dark, which staff link to the giant green being that key 004-12 shows its users, a sight that leaves most of them catatonic, clawing at their eyes, or dead. The late addendum on a box that erases anything locked inside, and somehow affects someone's dreams, along with a redacted hint that the keys may fit other doors, leaves the mystery wider than it started.
